newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Non-governmental organisations seek say in APEC.
newsitem.headline: Non-governmental organisations seek say in APEC.

text.p: Non-governmental organisations meeting in Manila on the sidelines of the APEC forum's annual summit said on Wednesday they should be given an advisory role by the regional trade group.

Nicanor Perlas, chairman of the Caucus on Development NGO (CODE-NGO) which includes several activist and community organisations in the region and organised the Manila meeting, said a council made up of NGOs, representatives of the church and the media should act as advisers to APEC.

Leaders from the 18 member economies in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum are due to meet in Manila on Sunday and in nearby Subic Bay the following day for their annual summit. The summit is preceded by a series of meetings of senior officials and ministers.

Perlas said the proposed new council should be accorded the same status as the APEC Business Advisory Council, or ABAC, which consists of some 50 business executives chosen by APEC leaders to give advice on how to achieve the group's goal of liberalising trade in the region by the year 2020.
Unlike some other groups critical of APEC, the CODE-NGO meeting has sought to avoid a confrontational relationship with APEC organisers.
At least three leftist groups have called for "anti-APEC" meetings, which the Philippine government says are aimed at disrupting the APEC meet.
Perlas said his group would meet President Fidel Ramos on Thursday to present their recommendations.

"We will ask the president to consider the formation of some form of institutional mechanism in APEC where there can be a formal interface between APEC leaders and leaders of civic society," Perlas said.
